steps.what: Identify parcels, historical references and legal records needed for the survey
Search archive indexes and retrieve matching survey records and land titles
Read source records and resolve relevance, gaps and boundary interpretation

tasks.design: Use native batch index search in {OTHER}, the land-record archive, for surveyor-verified identifiers. Keep reading original documents and interpreting boundary evidence with the surveyor in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated index searches are separate from substantive record interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable archive identifiers can support repeatable retrieval without inferring legal boundaries.
tasks.still_hard: Historical parcel changes, missing records and conflicting descriptions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a record can and cannot establish about a boundary.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive retrieval; legal and survey interpretation remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Parcel lineage and authoritative source limits

evidence.claim: Kadaster reports OCR and AI support for historical deeds and field sketches with people confirming results; no measured search saving is established.
The identifier-based retrieval design and time split are unmeasured assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is record research, excluding field measurement, final boundary determination and official registration.

The surveyor captures jurisdiction, parcel references, date range and known deed or survey identifiers in s1, including manual reconciliation of historical references. No free structured parcel lineage is assumed.

The archive custodian produces the authoritative identifier index through existing archival work; added mapping and access maintenance is counted. Unmatched, ambiguous or unavailable entries require manual archive research in s3.
Test native archive search and exports before custom code; no OCR text is treated as an authoritative boundary conclusion.
unknowns: Archive batch access and identifier coverage
Current search effort and historical reference gaps
research_questions: Does batch retrieval reduce total research time after original-source reading and missing-record work?

already_counted.description: Query capture and substantive source interpretation

incremental.description: Archive access and identifier mapping maintenance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R70 gross30 minus8 upkeep gives net22. Range0-5 allows incomplete archive access or already efficient searches to absorb most retrieval opportunity.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify survey data and specify charts, maps, records and document requirements
Prepare survey charts, plots, maps and records from the verified specification
Check survey meaning, geometry and completeness and accept the exact deliverable set

tasks.design: Configure native drawing and report templates in {OTHER}, the surveying and mapping system, linked to {DOCS}. The surveyor supplies verified geometry and conclusions and accepts the exact generated deliverables before separate external issue.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same verified data is assembled into multiple output formats.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports and templates can repeat explicit drawing and report rules.
tasks.still_hard: Boundary meaning, reference-system errors and misleading map presentation.
tasks.human_edge: Ensure a technically correct drawing communicates a defensible survey conclusion.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated output assembly; survey responsibility remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: Trimble Business Center produces adjustment reports; this supports a native reporting capability, not automatic legal survey conclusions.
The broader template design, shares and savings are unmeasured model-knowledge assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is deliverable preparation after separately counted field measurement and survey conclusions; external issue and registration are excluded.

Field survey staff produce point identifiers, coordinates, units, reference system, observation provenance and quality information in existing measurement work. In s1 the surveyor captures and verifies dataset versions, accepted geometry, labels, scale, uncertainty notes, required formats and conclusions; full manual extraction and checking remains.
Missing control information or unresolved boundary meaning stops generation for manual resolution. No free accepted-boundary or final-map-ready flag is assumed.
Test native mapping exports and report templates before custom code; existing automatic drawing runtime earns no new saving.
unknowns: Geometry quality and manual assembly effort
research_questions: Can native generation reduce active preparation after full survey and presentation checks?

already_counted.description: Specification capture and final deliverable checking

approvals.approved_version: Exact source versions, geometry, maps, charts, notes and document set; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R60 gross40 minus8 upkeep gives net32. Range0-8 allows existing templates or complex boundary presentation to absorb most assembly opportunity.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Establish fixed points using geodetic and engineering instruments and field checks

tasks.design: Retain field point establishment and instrument checks with the surveyor. Data in {OTHER}, the surveying system, informs the work without establishing a physical point by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stable, suitable physical points require on-site assessment and measurement.
tasks.enabler_now: No supplied capability removes the stated field work.
tasks.still_hard: Access, stability, geometry and instrument setup errors.
tasks.human_edge: Choose and verify usable control in real conditions.
tasks.altitude: Field time and responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Establishing a fixed physical survey point requires field measurement and judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is physical point establishment, excluding later map preparation and adjustment reporting.
The surveyor produces point observations, setup and location details in s1; no free stable-point or valid-control flag is assumed.
Use existing instruments and native records before custom tools; no additional system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new process is introduced.
unknowns: Site access and existing control quality
research_questions: Which conditions prevent a point from remaining usable?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0; physical establishment and checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Train assistants and helpers and direct survey or map drafting work

tasks.design: Keep demonstration, feedback and direction with the surveyor. Existing procedures in {DOCS} support training without replacing observed competence checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assistants need feedback on actual performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital instructions do not establish competence or safe execution.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting misunderstanding before it affects measurements or drawings.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt instruction and intervene at the right moment.
tasks.altitude: Training and direction time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Direct training requires observation and adaptive feedback; no saving is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is the surveyor's direct training and supervision time, excluding assistants' labour and separate material preparation.
The surveyor observes performance and identifies learning needs during s1; no free structured competence flag is assumed.
Use existing procedures before custom tools; no new software is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no changed process is introduced.
research_questions: Which errors require direct demonstration rather than written instructions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0; direct training and supervision remain.

reach: Coordinate provenance with records officers and cartographic technicians
